title: Scanning a doubled bit string
statement: Let $z$ and $w$ be finite bit strings, let $r$ be a natural number, and let $�phi$ be either the initial scan phase or the separator phase. Suppose $z$ is the concatenation of a prefix, the string obtained by repeating each bit of $w$ twice, and a suffix. Starting with the input head at the end of the prefix, the first work tape empty, the second work tape containing $r$ marks from cell zero, both work heads at cell $r$, and empty output, after $2|w|$ steps the machine is in the configuration prescribed by folding the scan update over $w$: its phase and mark count are the resulting pair, its input head has advanced by $2|w|$ positions, and its work tapes, heads, and output are as initially specified.
hypotheses_covered: $\phi$ is the initial scan phase or separator phase
$z$ is a prefix followed by the doubled word $w$ and a suffix
the prefix length is a valid input position
the prefix length plus $2|w|$ is a valid input position
